pending_commit.commit_message: netperf_runner: fixup error handling for 'None' results We access the 'result.exit_status' field before checking if it's None. That's broken. Reorganize the ignore_failures vs. !ignore_failures logic a bit, and add a new TestFail() condition for when we get no results and haven't asked for 'ignore_failures=True'. BUG=chromium:629137 TEST=network_AttenuatedPerf, with high attenuation (causing association failures on certain boards) Change-Id: I7881391eed3bb10a8b58573e1567a6c3e5aaea0b Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/696267 Reviewed-by: Harpreet Grewal <harpreet@chromium.org>

netperf: limit extent of retries, timeout delays When run with 'ignore_failures' (e.g., with AttenuatedPerf), we forgive all failure and just wait until the end to collect a None result. This is pointless and time-wasting, especially on attenuated tests, where we ramp up attenuation until the client gets abysmal performance (and likely disconnects from the AP eventually). We should not keep trying to get 10 samples (MEASUREMENT_MAX_SAMPLES) when we see multiple None results (i.e., errors). Limit this to 2 failures, and abort on the 3rd. Also, CL:217970 increased the netperf timeout from a 10 second margin (on top of test time) to 120 seconds, with no explanation. This seems excessively high for a 10-second test. And note that we do hit this timeout sometimes, when running AttenuatedPerf. So let's decrease that to 60 seconds, which should still be conservative, but should save us several times that much on some tests, since netperf sessions often include multiple retries. BUG=none TEST=network_WiFi_AttenuatedPerf Change-Id: I7712fbcb39176c28b037231bb6c4708579672ec4 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/696671 Reviewed-by: Harpreet Grewal <harpreet@chromium.org>

network_WiFi_AttenuatedPerf: autodetect/report max attenuation CL:286195 changed both the min and max attenuation values we would use. This artificially restricted us to a range of +20 dB, which doesn't really cover as much range as we'd like, in some cases. Let's try to bump that back up. However, in testing more extreme attenuation, I've found that at least on some DUTs, we can't even connect to the AP. Our netperf code isn't able to promptly handle this condition, as the current logic tries for 10 samples (or failures), each consisting of up to 3 retries, and a 2 minute timeout. That means it will take 1 hour for a run to complete in the null case where we haven't even associated correctly. We should probably improve the netperf logic to handle this a little better too, but as a first step, we can check for a connection before kicking off a session. So this CL: (a) adds a basic connectivity test for each attenuation level (b) stops testing an attenuation level if any netperf session returns no result (c) logs (and reports to the keyval storage) the maximum attenuation reached (d) expands the theoretical max attenuation to 100dB, instead of "start + 20" Example runs now look something like this: INFO | autoserv| RvR test: current attenuation = 79 dB INFO | autoserv| Waiting for AttenuatedPerf_a_4fgeb_ch1 to reach one of ['ready', 'portal', 'online']... INFO | autoserv| ...ended up in state 'online' (success) after 0.007059 seconds. INFO | autoserv| Pinging from the client. INFO | autoserv| Could not establish connection at 79 dB INFO | autoserv| Error: Ping command failed with code=1 INFO | autoserv| Running time 968.1 seconds. INFO | autoserv| Reached attenuation of: 75 dB (signal -76 dBm) BUG=none TEST=network_WiFi_AttenuatedPerf, see expanded atten values tested Change-Id: Ie435ecc80ac78017dc9f003dd2cf0c4ef446323b Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/695707 Reviewed-by: Harpreet Grewal <harpreet@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kirtika Ruchandani <kirtika@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: mwifiex: avoid storing random_mac in private Application will keep track of whether MAC address randomization is enabled or not during scan. But at present driver is storing 'random_mac' in mwifiex_private which implies even after scan is done driver has some reference to the earlier 'scan request'. To avoid this, make use of 'mac_addr' variable in 'scan_request' to store 'random_mac'. This structure will be freed by cfg80211 once scan is done. Signed-off-by: Ganapathi Bhat <gbhat@marvell.com> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> (cherry picked from git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/kvalo/wireless-drivers-next.git master commit e251a882c0bae39d3d31efe993e977104605a9b3) pre-cq-configs: mixed-wificell-pre-cq BUG=b:37088079 TEST=Ran below command and confirmed we could see random MAC address while scanning: iw dev mlan0 scan randomise=<addr>/<mask> Change-Id: I4f7e81468d714909eb1fd95f60afd8dbf32dfef5 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/700317 Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

update_engine: Add Flush() to FileDescriptor This patch adds Flush() function to the file descriptor. This function should be called after each operation in order to ensure that data resides to disk before any checkpointing happen. In addition, if any future file descriptor that caches the data is added, this ensures integrity of written data.
